items.title: Spanish pensioner whose eviction sparked nationwide protests dies
items.summary: Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years in September.
items.content:
An elderly woman whose eviction sparked nationwide protests over Spain's housing crisis and a political row that triggered early elections has died, according to Madrid's tenants union.

Maricarmen Abascal, 87, was forcibly removed on a stretcher from her apartment of more than 70 years on 23 September after she was unable to afford steep rent increases.

The company that owned the flat later offered to allow her to return at a lower rate - but she was unable to sign an agreement as she had been admitted to hospital.

Announcing her death, Madrid Tenants' Union said Abascal's situation marked "a turning point in the history of this country".

The 87-year-old and her eviction became a symbol for Spain's housing crisis. The Socialist-led government sought to respond to the protests but its bid to push through urgent housing measures failed, prompting Prime Minister Pedro Sánchez to call snap elections.

"Speculation costs lives, and today rent profiteering has finished killing our colleague Maricarmen," said union spokeswoman Alicia del Río.

The 87-year-old was already in fragile health at the time of her eviction and she was admitted to Madrid's Gregorio Marañón Hospital, sending messages of support to protesters from her hospital bed.

When news of her death reached Puerta del Sol - the Madrid square where thousands have camped since her eviction to demand more affordable housing - there was a collective gasp, followed by a minute of silence.

Dozens of candles were lit around the square, with more laid out to form an altar to Abascal in front of the headquarters of the Community of Madrid government.

Messages laid at the scene read "it's not a death, it's a killing", "the fight will continue" and "Maricarmen, the grandmother of the whole country", among others.

Maricarmen Abascal's father had first rented the flat in Madrid's Retiro district in 1956 and she continued as the tenant after her parents died, during which time there was a cap on the rent.

The area has become increasingly sought-after, and Urbagestión, the company that bought the property in 2018, increased the rent from €500 per month (£428; $572) to €2,650 (£2,280; $3,020).

Rental costs in Madrid have soared by more than 100% over the last decade, according to property site Idealista.

The company later offered to reduce this to €1,650 - still €300 more than Abascal's monthly pension.

Three earlier attempts to evict her had been blocked by the courts and her case attracted widespread support from the public and celebrities.

Prime Minister Sánchez's minority government announced two emergency decrees to tackle the housing crisis, but they were rejected in Congress last week , and on Monday he called elections for 29 November. Opponents pointed out he had had eight years in office to respond to the issue.

Tens of thousands of people took to the streets last weekend in cities across the country, as protests continued.

"All my love goes to Maricarmen's family and loved ones," Sánchez said on Wednesday night. "A hug as well to everyone who today feels this loss as their own."

The leader of the opposition People's Party, Alberto Núñez Feijóo, also sent his condolences, appealing for her death not to be politicised: "No campaign, no parties, no self-interested exploitation. No more stones in the wall.

"In the face of a person's death, only respect is in order," he added.

The Madrid Tenants' Union said the events surrounding her eviction represented a turning point in the country's history, but added that the cost to get to this point had been "too high".

In one video recorded from her hospital bed following her eviction, Maricarmen said: "I haven't managed to defend my home, but I have fought so that others can learn to fight for what's theirs."

A few hundred people marched from Puerta del Sol to parliament on Wednesday night, chanting "we will not tolerate a single eviction more" and "the fight will continue, Maricarmen is still alive".

There were other chants against the police. Many protesters believed that police had been complicit in the evictions, as under court orders they have to remove tenants who have been served eviction notices.

After a couple of hours, the chants near Congress gave way to another minute of silence. Then, a big collective shout of "murderers".

One protester told the BBC that people would remain in the square "as long as necessary".

Earlier on Wednesday, unions had called a general strike to take place on 11 November, demanding housing reforms.

The public outcry over Abascal's situation exposed the deep political divisions in Spain.

The political right argued that the government's attempt to intervene in the housing market would have led to fewer homes being rented and would have raised prices further.

Sánchez said on Monday he needed "a broader progressive majority" that could "overcome the resistance of the elites" to push through reforms.

However, other issues unrelated to housing, including numerous corruption scandals linked to his party, and pressures relating to the cost of living and immigration, have also caused him problems.

Most opinion polls suggest the conservative People's Party is likely to emerge as the largest party in the next election. However, they would be expected to need the support of the hard-right Vox party, currently third in the polls, to form a government.

Spanish PM Sánchez calls early election after housing protests

Dramatic eviction of woman aged 87 highlights Spain's housing shortage

items.title: Le differenze tra il caso del gioielliere graziato e quello di Roggero
items.summary: Guido Gianni ha passato già molto tempo in carcere, e la sua domanda di grazia ha seguito le normali procedure
items.content:
Il presidente della Repubblica Sergio Mattarella ha concesso una grazia parziale a Guido Gianni, un gioielliere di Nicolosi, in provincia di Catania, condannato a 12 anni e 4 mesi per aver ucciso due rapinatori nel 2008. La sua storia è stata paragonata subito a quella di Mario Roggero, il gioielliere piemontese condannato per un caso simile e per cui la Lega chiede da mesi la grazia. Pur avendo alcune somiglianze, tra le vicende ci sono delle differenze sostanziali, innanzitutto nel modo in cui la procedura di grazia di Gianni è avvenuta e nel periodo di pena scontato.

Gianni ha 66 anni e ha già scontato cinque anni e tre mesi. Con la grazia parziale gli restano meno di quattro anni da scontare. Sotto questa soglia il tribunale di sorveglianza può concedergli l’affidamento in prova ai servizi sociali: è una misura alternativa al carcere, con cui il condannato può vivere fuori e seguire un programma controllato dagli assistenti sociali. Mattarella ha esplicitato e quindi suggerito questa possibilità nell’annuncio della grazia. Gianni ora è ai domiciliari perché ha dei problemi di salute, un’altra delle ragioni che hanno motivato la procedura di grazia.

Il 18 febbraio 2008 tre uomini entrarono nella gioielleria che Gianni gestiva con la moglie, Maria Angela Distefano. Gianni era nel retrobottega. I rapinatori picchiarono la moglie e la minacciarono con una pistola: si scoprì poi che era un giocattolo, ma non aveva il tappo rosso che permette di riconoscere le armi finte. Gianni aveva una pistola regolarmente detenuta. Sparò prima due colpi in aria, poi contro i rapinatori: uccise Davide Laudani e Sebastiano Catania, che avevano 21 anni, e ferì il terzo, Fabio Pappalardo. Secondo i giudici, Laudani e Catania furono colpiti alla schiena mentre scappavano. Per questo a Gianni non fu riconosciuta la legittima difesa.

Al processo gli avvocati chiesero l’assoluzione. Sostennero che Gianni non fosse in grado di intendere e di volere per lo shock e che per questo si dovesse applicare la legittima difesa nella formulazione introdotta dalla riforma del 2019 , quella che tiene conto del “grave turbamento” di chi si difende in casa propria o nel suo negozio. Il pubblico ministero chiese 17 anni di reclusione, il giudice condannò Gianni a 13 anni, pena ridotta a 12 anni e 4 mesi in appello.

Mario Roggero è stato condannato a 14 anni e 9 mesi per una vicenda simile. Il 28 aprile 2021 uccise a colpi di pistola due rapinatori che avevano appena derubato il suo negozio a Grinzane Cavour. Durante le indagini Roggero sostenne di avere sparato per legittima difesa durante un tentativo di rapina. Si scoprì però che li aveva inseguiti e che aveva sparato loro quando già si trovavano lontano dal negozio, in fuga.

La procedura per ottenere la grazia stabilisce che la domanda deve essere presentata dal condannato, da un familiare o dal suo avvocato al ministero della Giustizia, che raccoglie le informazioni, tra cui il parere del magistrato di sorveglianza, e poi trasmette la pratica alla presidenza della Repubblica. Per Gianni la procedura è stata seguita in questo modo: la domanda è arrivata a Mattarella con il parere favorevole del magistrato di sorveglianza e del ministro della Giustizia, Carlo Nordio. Per prassi, dopo averle esaminate, Mattarella acconsente alle domande di grazia quando hanno già ricevuto questa doppia approvazione.

Nel caso di Roggero, invece, Nordio ha avviato l’istruttoria di sua iniziativa, prima della presentazione della domanda. In quell’occasione Mattarella ha convocato Nordio per precisare i limiti dei poteri del ministro della Giustizia e per ribadire che solo il presidente della Repubblica ha il potere di concedere la grazia. Quell’iniziativa, poi, non ha avuto più alcun seguito.

C’è poi la questione del tempo, perché Gianni ha scontato più di cinque anni, quasi metà della pena. Roggero invece è detenuto da meno di tre mesi. Concedere la grazia subito dopo una condanna definitiva è una cosa su cui la presidenza della Repubblica è sempre stata cauta. Come ha ricordato Concetto Vecchio su Repubblica , nel 2008 l’allora presidente Giorgio Napolitano spiegò che concedere la grazia all’ex funzionario di polizia Bruno Contrada poco tempo dopo la sentenza della Cassazione sarebbe diventato una specie di quarto grado di giudizio.

L’ultima differenza riguarda il pentimento. Gianni si è sempre detto pentito di aver ucciso i rapinatori, Roggero invece ha detto più volte che rifarebbe quello che ha fatto. Soltanto poco prima di entrare in carcere ha detto ai giornalisti di essere pentito e di aver reagito solo per paura. Inoltre, come riporta la Sicilia nella cronaca del processo, subito dopo la condanna di primo grado Gianni disse di voler rispettare la decisione dei giudici e di non voler fare appello, per cambiare idea solo successivamente.

items.title: HPV: un altro importante beneficio del vaccino
items.summary: HPV: un altro importante beneficio del vaccino
items.content:
Lo stesso vaccino che sta portando alla quasi eradicazione del tumore al collo dell'utero - quello contro il Papilloma virus umano (HPV) - offre una protezione sostanziale anche contro i tumori del distretto testa-collo.
La conferma arriva da uno studio condotto sui dati di 1,4 milioni di persone: la vaccinazione contro l'HPV è un importante strumento di prevenzione delle forme di cancro che interessano la bocca, il naso e la gola, e funziona in special modo contro il carcinoma orofaringeo, un tumore maligno della parte media della gola di cui l'infezione da Papillomavirus è una delle cause principali. I risultati sono stati pubblicati sull'International Journal of Infectious Diseases.. Come cambia il rischio tra vaccinati e non. Lo studio condotto da due Università di Taiwan ha analizzato i dati tratti dalle cartelle cliniche anonimizzate di 66 organizzazioni sanitarie statunitensi, relative a pazienti tra i 9 e i 45 anni e corrispondenti al periodo 2011-2024. Gli scienziati hanno confrontato il rischio di tumori testa-collo in 716.630 individui che erano stati vaccinati contro l'HPV con quello di 716.630 soggetti di controllo non vaccinati, ma con profili di età, sesso e malattie pregresse corrispondenti.. Nel gruppo di vaccinati si sono verificati 40 casi di tumori testa-collo, e in quello dei non vaccinati 130: la vaccinazione contro l'HPV è risultata associata quindi a una riduzione del rischio generale di queste forme di cancro del 68,5%. Per un tumore in particolare, il carcinoma a cellule squamose dell'orofaringe, si è osservata una protezione associata particolarmente marcata, con il rischio praticamente azzerato nei vaccinati.. Il Papilloma virus umano e i tumori testa-collo. I tumori che colpiscono l'area tra testa e collo (e dunque il cavo orale, la lingua, la faringe, la laringe, le cavità nasali) interessano ogni anno circa 660.000 nuove persone, 10.000 delle quali in Italia. In oltre 7 casi su 10 sono causati dal consumo prolungato di tabacco o alcol, ma l'HPV è un altro fattore di rischio riconosciuto: in circa il 31% delle persone con tumori dell'orofaringe è stata riscontrata un'infezione da Papilloma virus (in particolare dell'HPV-16, uno dei più comuni ceppi ad alto rischio).
I sopravvissuti ai tumori testa-collo si trovano spesso ad affrontare conseguenze permanenti legate alla malattia e alle cure per eradicarla, come difficoltà di deglutizione, problemi nel senso del gusto e dell'olfatto, disagi estetici, alterazioni della voce o difficoltà a parlare correttamente.. Finora la maggior parte della ricerca scientifica si è concentrata sui benefici del vaccino contro l'HPV nella prevenzione di tumori cervicali e anogenitali.
Nei Paesi che si sono impegnati per primi in campagne di vaccinazioni di massa nelle ragazze e nei ragazzi di età precoce (cioè prima dell'inizio dell'attività sessuale, 11-13 anni), come Regno Unito e Australia, l'effetto del vaccino unito a quello dello screening precoce (Pap-test) e dell'immunità di gregge, che fa calare i contagi da HPV anche nei non vaccinati, hanno portato a una riduzione dei casi di tumore al collo dell'utero di circa il 90% rispetto alle generazioni di donne non vaccinate.
Inoltre, per effetto del vaccino la circolazione dell'HPV si è ridotta ormai a tal punto, che l'Australia ha stimato di poter arrivare un giorno all'eradicazione del tumore al collo dell'utero. . Meno lampanti erano le prove dell'efficacia della vaccinazione contro l'HPV nella prevenzione dei tumori testa collo. Secondo il nuovo studio, la protezione offerta dal vaccino su queste forme di cancro persiste per almeno 13 anni dalla somministrazione, e i risultati dovrebbero incoraggiare chi si occupa di salute pubblica a promuovere la vaccinazione contro l'HPV anche per ridurre l'incidenza dei tumori che interessano bocca, naso e gola..

items.title: La Corte di Cassazione ha confermato le due condanne e tre assoluzioni per il disastro ferroviario di Andria
items.content:
La Corte di Cassazione ha reso definitive due condanne e tre assoluzioni per il disastro ferroviario di Andria , del 12 luglio 2016, quando 23 persone morirono in uno scontro tra due treni lungo la linea ferroviaria Bari-Barletta.

Le condanne confermate sono quelle nei confronti dei due ferrovieri Vito Piccarreta e Nicola Lorizzo, rispettivamente capostazione di Andria e capotreno del treno partito da Andria e diretto a Corato: la Cassazione ha confermato l’assoluzione di Ferrotramviaria, la società privata che gestiva i due treni, e di due suoi dirigenti. Le motivazioni saranno disponibili nelle prossime settimane: la sentenza di secondo grado, comunque, aveva stabilito che l’incidente era stato provocato da un errore umano.

Tecnicamente, la Cassazione ha respinto alcuni ricorsi presentati contro la sentenza d’appello, rendendo quindi definitive le due condanne e le tre assoluzioni contestate. nel processo erano state 14 in tutto .

items.title: Qualcuno ha manomesso la segreteria telefonica della Corea del Nord all’ONU
items.summary: Per giorni ha risposto una voce femminile che imitava l’accento asiatico e prendeva in giro il paese e il suo governo
items.content:
«Accidenti. Oh mio Dio. Non porti fuori la spazzatura. Beh, in Corea del Nord siamo tutti spazzatura». Iniziava così lo strano messaggio registrato che si è sentito per giorni quando si chiamava al telefono la missione permanente della Corea del Nord alle Nazioni Unite. Qualcuno aveva manomesso la segreteria telefonica: la voce era quella di una donna che parlava in inglese imitando in modo goffo e razzista un accento asiatico, e le cose che diceva erano molto critiche verso la Corea del Nord e il suo governo.

La prima ad accorgersi del messaggio era stata la CNN a fine settembre. Il Post ha chiamato il numero più volte. Le prime aveva trovato la segreteria con lo stesso messaggio, poi aveva risposto un uomo: aveva confermato che si trattava del numero della missione permanente della Corea del Nord all’ONU, ma si era rifiutato di rispondere alle domande sul contenuto del messaggio. Nelle chiamate successive aveva risposto di nuovo la segreteria, con lo stesso messaggio.

Dopo la frase iniziale, il messaggio proseguiva: «La Corea del Nord è la miglior Corea [North Korea is best Korea] e lo sappiamo perché non diamo da mangiare al nostro popolo». È un riferimento ironico alla grave e cronica crisi alimentare del paese: secondo le stime del Programma alimentare mondiale dell’ONU più del 40 per cento della popolazione della Corea del Nord è denutrita .

Poi il messaggio scherzava su Kim Jong Un, dittatore della Corea del Nord: «Se vuoi parlare con Kim Jong Un, devi parlare con me. Io parlo con lui, poi noi parliamo con te, e magari, prima o poi, qualcuno verrà sfamato». Alla fine interveniva una voce automatica, con la frase che ci si aspetterebbe da una segreteria telefonica: «Impossibile ricevere un messaggio. La casella vocale è piena. Per lasciare un messaggio a qualcun altro, premi due».

Da mercoledì sera sembra che il problema sia stato sistemato perché il messaggio non si sente più. Si sente solo un beep.

Il Palazzo di Vetro a New York, la sede delle Nazioni Unite (UN Photo/Rick Bajornas)

La Corea del Nord non ha un’ambasciata negli Stati Uniti. La missione all’ONU è la sua unica sede diplomatica in territorio americano e per molto tempo è stata uno dei pochi punti di contatto tra i due governi, il cosiddetto “canale di New York”. La missione per esempio ebbe un ruolo importante nelle trattative del 1994 sul programma nucleare nordcoreano, alla fine delle quali il regime nordcoreano si impegnò a congelarlo. L’accordo però si ruppe nel 2002 e da diversi anni i due paesi hanno perso anche i pochi contatti diplomatici che avevano. Oggi il “canale di New York” è praticamente inattivo.

Le missioni o rappresentanze permanenti alle Nazioni Unite sono le sedi dei diplomatici e dei funzionari che lavorano all’ONU per conto dei rispettivi paesi. Si trovano per lo più vicino alla sede centrale dell’organizzazione, il Palazzo di Vetro, nella parte orientale di Manhattan, a New York. Quella della Corea del Nord è al tredicesimo piano di un anonimo edificio di una ventina di piani, che ospita anche le sedi diplomatiche di altri paesi, a cinque minuti a piedi dal Palazzo di Vetro.

Secondo il sito del Servizio di protocollo e collegamento delle Nazioni Unite nella missione lavorano 23 persone. La CNN ci è andata per chiedere spiegazioni sul messaggio: un membro dello staff, a cui è stato fatto ascoltare per intero, ha detto che quello non era il numero della missione e ha chiuso la porta. Pochi giorni dopo, però, la missione ha diffuso il testo del discorso tenuto dal viceministro degli Esteri nordcoreano all’Assemblea generale dell’ONU di settembre: aveva quello stesso numero sulla prima pagina.

Il palazzo dove si trova la missione permanente della Corea del Nord a New York (Google Street View)

Non si sa chi abbia manomesso la segreteria telefonica e senza accedere ai registri delle chiamate della missione è impossibile scoprirlo. Modificare il messaggio potrebbe comunque non essere stato difficile. Martin Vigo, esperto di sicurezza informatica, ha spiegato alla CNN che molti utenti non modificano il codice di accesso alla segreteria e tengono quello predefinito fornito dall’operatore, che in alcuni casi corrisponde alle ultime quattro cifre del numero di telefono.

Secondo Vigo, indovinare questi codici di poche cifre è facile ed economico: con servizi di chiamata automatizzati si possono infatti provare migliaia di combinazioni in poco tempo e senza spendere molto.

items.title: Come sta la donna sopravvissuta a due iniezioni letali negli Stati Uniti
items.summary: Gli avvocati di Christa Pike hanno detto che è «confusa e arrabbiata»: parla con difficoltà ed è in condizioni gravi
items.content:
Mercoledì gli avvocati di Christa Pike, la donna statunitense sopravvissuta in Tennessee a due iniezioni letali durante l’esecuzione della sua condanna a morte, hanno parlato delle sue condizioni in una conferenza stampa. Hanno detto che è cosciente ma ancora molto confusa, e che fa fatica a muoversi e a parlare. Hanno aggiunto che Pike sa cosa le è successo ed è «arrabbiata».

Anche se è sveglia, le sue condizioni sono gravi: ha un coagulo di sangue in un braccio, la polmonite, non è in grado di deglutire, non può muovere le braccia e ha le mani ingrossate come «due guanti in lattice gonfiati», ha detto uno dei suoi avvocati, Randy Spivey.

Pike ha 50 anni ed era stata condannata a morte nel 1996 per omicidio. Durante l’esecuzione, il 30 settembre, era sopravvissuta a due dosi di pentobarbital, un sedativo molto potente che rallenta l’attività del sistema nervoso centrale e che in dosi massicce provoca la morte: non ci sono altri casi noti di questo tipo. Era stata portata via in ambulanza dal penitenziario di Riverbend e ricoverata in condizioni molto gravi.

I suoi avvocati avevano spiegato che Pike era incosciente e attaccata a un respiratore, e che aveva subìto lesioni importanti a entrambe le braccia. Poi si era svegliata, inaspettatamente: si riteneva fosse in uno stato di morte cerebrale, e il suo risveglio era stato definito « senza precedenti dal punto di vista medico ».

L’ipotesi principale, avanzata dagli avvocati, è che i funzionari del carcere incaricati di somministrare i farmaci utilizzati per le iniezioni letali, che non sono medici né infermieri, abbiano sbagliato a posizionare l’ago nel braccio e non siano quindi riusciti a iniettare il farmaco nelle vene di Pike, che sono molto sottili .

Le condizioni della donna sono state rese note al termine di un’udienza in cui la giudice ha stabilito che lo stato del Tennessee dovrà conservare tutta la documentazione sul tentativo di esecuzione. Sono documenti importanti per la causa legale nata dal suo caso: gli avvocati di Pike hanno chiesto che la condanna a morte sia commutata in ergastolo, ma il governatore del Tennessee per il momento non ha risposto. Non è chiaro se, quando Pike si sarà ripresa, verrà nuovamente eseguita la sua condanna a morte.

items.title: Margaret Hamilton, whose software helped land Apollo 11 on the Moon, dies at 90
items.summary: Pioneering computer scientist led the development of the software for Nasa's Apollo mission and was awarded the Presidential Medal of Freedom.
items.content:
The computer scientist behind groundbreaking research that helped land Nasa's astronauts on the Moon, has died aged 90.

Margaret Hamilton was a trailblazer in her field, leading the team who developed the software for Nasa's Apollo missions, which coined the term "software engineering".

Hamilton's former employer, the Massachusetts Institute of Technology (MIT), confirmed her death, adding she died on 30 September.

"To say Hamilton was a pioneer - to say she was ahead of her time - would be a dramatic understatement," MIT said in its statement, before acknowledging that she was a software engineer before it was mainstream.

Hamilton worked at MIT from 1959 until the mid-1970s and managed the Software Engineering Division.

It was in this division that she led a team of engineers writing and testing all onboard in-flight software for Nasa's Apollo 11 project that guided US astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin to land safely on the Moon.

"I was attracted both by the sheer idea and the fact that it had never been done before. I was the first programmer to join and the first woman they hired," she told the Guardian in 2019.

In 1969, moments before the historic Apollo 11 Moon landing, an onboard computer raised an alarm, signalling an error was occurring.

The error detected the computer was overloaded, and for a moment it looked like the complex landing might not be achieved.

But Hamilton and her team had planned for such an error by engineering "priority-driven software" to shut down any background tasks and favour the most important - the Moon landing - according to MIT.

The team's famous software engineering was immortalised in a 1969 photograph of Hamilton standing beside the stack of printed code that towered beside her.

In 2016, Hamilton's life work was honoured by Barack Obama with the Presidential Medal of Freedom for her contribution to science and space travel.

At the time, Obama said Hamilton "symbolises that generation of unsung women who helped send humankind into space".

Hamilton, born in Indiana in 1936, first studied mathematics at the University of Michigan in 1955 before moving to Earlham College where she got a BA in mathematics in 1958.

She then moved to Boston, Massachusetts, a year later with her husband and originally took the job at MIT to support her husband during his law degree.

From the 1970s onwards, Hamilton used her expertise to found her own software businesses, including Hamilton Technologies, which is still based in Massachusetts.

"We are saddened by her death, but grateful for the opportunity to have celebrated her extraordinary achievements throughout her long life", Earlham College said in a statement on social media.

"Her pioneering spirit and remarkable legacy will continue to inspire generations of Earlhamites," the statement said.

Hamilton is survived by her daughter, a son-in-law, two grandsons and four great-grandchildren, according to MIT.

items.title: US and Lebanon protecting wanted Syrian general, BBC finds
items.summary: Bassam al-Hassan is being sheltered in return for information - including about abducted US reporter Austin Tice.
items.content:
A former Syrian general wanted for crimes against humanity , external is being bankrolled and protected by the US and Lebanese authorities, a BBC News investigation has found.

Bassam al-Hassan, who oversaw Syria's chemical weapons programme and was a senior adviser to former President Bashar al-Assad, is being harboured in Lebanon following the Assad regime's collapse in 2024.

An investigation by the BBC and the US broadcaster NPR has discovered that Hassan has been allowed to remain there under an arrangement involving the FBI, and other US and Lebanese authorities. This is because of his willingness to provide information about the abduction of American journalist Austin Tice in Syria in 2012, as well as additional intelligence, we have been told.

Last month the BBC revealed Tice's abduction had been a planned operation , with Hassan in the chain of command.

Officials from two different branches of Syria's new government have told the BBC they want Hassan returned to face trial, but that US authorities want him kept in Lebanon, and they say there is little Damascus can do about this.

We asked the FBI, the CIA and Lebanon's General Directorate of General Security to comment on our findings. Only the FBI responded, declining to comment and instead directing us to a past statement that said its focus remained on establishing the facts around the Tice case and securing his return.

In response to our findings, Phil Elwood, spokesperson for the Tice family said: "If what you are saying is true, the fact that our tax dollars are being used to furnish a comfortable life for someone associated with the use of chemical weapons on Syrian civilians, who claims to have had Austin Tice executed, is offensive.

"This is nothing less than aiding and abetting the escape of a wanted war criminal. The Syrians deserve justice and he should be returned to stand trial."

Josh Baker enters a dangerous world of fear, greed and betrayal as he uncovers what happened in one of the biggest missing-person cases of our time - the abduction of Austin Tice.

As part of a years-long investigation featured in the new BBC podcast: Where is Austin Tice? the BBC has reviewed a detailed record of a meeting between Hassan, FBI and CIA representatives, and Lebanese security officials, where Tice's case is discussed.

In it, Hassan is offered "residency", "protection" and help securing his "living needs" in return for information, primarily about Tice.

Sources with knowledge of the arrangement confirmed this was the case, and described to us how Hassan receives money from the US authorities through an intermediary, making it harder to trace. Hassan is sanctioned by the US government.

Yet people connected to the Tice investigation say they have seen little evidence it has significantly advanced since Hassan began providing information as part of this agreement. The deal is believed to have been struck in the spring of 2025.

Sources with knowledge of the investigation have expressed concerns that Hassan's arrangement with the US could continue indefinitely, at significant expense but with little gain.

Hassan is not the only Syrian regime official whose connection to the Tice case has seemingly afforded him financial payments or assistance for living abroad.

One former regime member said he had received money from the FBI multiple times in exchange for his co-operation on Tice's case. It was "not in his interest to share all the information all at once," he told the BBC, "in order to be able to drag out how long he can continue to receive payments from them [the US authorities]".

Another former regime member connected to the Tice case claimed he was living in Lebanon under the "patronage" of the US authorities, citing this as the reason he could not speak to us about Tice.

The BBC spoke to a former senior Lebanese intelligence official who confirmed that Lebanese intelligence does have arrangements with the Americans, and that these types of payments have and do take place when both agencies have overlap in cases, but said he had no knowledge of payments involving the Tice case.

Following the fall of the Assad regime in early December 2024, Hassan is believed to have initially escaped to Iran.

A Syrian businessman, with strong connections to both the former regime and the Lebanese authorities, told the BBC that negotiations had then taken place - involving the US, Lebanon, and Iran - to bring Hassan to Lebanon.

The businessman, who asked to remain anonymous, said Hassan was valuable, not only because of what he is believed to know about Tice, but because of his knowledge of Syria's chemical weapons programme and its military relationship with Iran - secrets that US intelligence was allegedly interested in.

Hassan told US investigators last year that Tice had been executed on former President Assad's orders, but several people with knowledge of the investigation have questioned the details of his account. Hassan has provided a potential location for Tice's remains, but when the site was searched, nothing was found - according to multiple sources familiar with the dig - casting doubt on the validity of some of Hassan's information.

There are questions, however, over how thoroughly the site was searched. Two sources who said they had intimate knowledge of the operation told the BBC that US authorities stopped digging before the search had been completed, possibly because of security concerns.

When the BBC managed to reach Hassan by phone last year to ask for an interview, he directed us to seek permission for him to speak from the FBI and CIA at the US embassy in Beirut.

Our investigation has found that other Syrian officials connected to the Tice case have also apparently found refuge abroad.

They include Mohammad Makhlouf, who reported to Hassan in Syria and was connected to Tice's detention - now believed to be residing in Lebanon. And Sakr Rustom, Hassan's nephew who was involved in Tice's abduction, now believed to be moving between the UAE and Lebanon. When the BBC attempted to speak to Rustom about Tice's case, he said he "preferred to focus on matters of the future".

Ghassan Nassour, a former general in Syria's Republican Guard, is said by former members of the National Defence Forces to have presided over the jail Tice was held in, and is believed to be living in the UAE with his family, we have been told.

items.title: Roomba in offerta per tutto ottobre: su irobot.it si parte da 149 euro
items.summary: Dodici modelli scontati fino al 31 ottobre, dai Combo d'ingresso ai Max con la base che lava il rullo. E dall'8 ottobre sei robot in offerta anche su Amazon ... Leggi tutto
items.content:
Per tutto ottobre il negozio online di iRobot mette in offerta 12 modelli dei suoi Roomb a , dal Roomba Combo 105 a 149 euro fino al prestanti Roomba Max 775 Combo con base AutoWash. Da oggi e fino al 31 ottobre, 6 modelli sono scontati anche su Amazon , in qualche caso a un prezzo ancora più basso. Se c'era un momento per smettere di passare l'aspirapolvere e il mocio, è questo.

Dodici voci possono spaventare, ma il listino si legge bene se lo si guarda per famiglie. Salendo di prezzo, il robot si prende in carico lavori che altrimenti resterebbero a noi, come svuotare il contenitore della polvere e lavare i panni sporchi. Scegliere significa anche capire fin dove si vuole delegare.

Quasi tutti i Roomba in offerta sono Combo, cioè aspirano e lavano il pavimento nella stessa passata . Si orientano con ClearView LiDAR , un sensore laser che misura le stanze e ne disegna la mappa. Il robot pulisce così per traiettorie ordinate , sa dove è già passato e nell'app si possono indicare le stanze da pulire.

La differenza vera la fa la base di ricarica. Quella AutoEmpty aspira a sua volta lo sporco raccolto dal robot e lo chiude in un sacchetto AllergenLock da 2,5 litri, che trattiene il 99% di pollini e muffe e va sostituito ogni tre mesi circa. La base AutoWash fa lo stesso lavoro e in più lava e asciuga i panni o il rullo lavapavimenti , così il robot riparte ogni volta pulito.

Un ultimo dato che può aiutare a orientarsi è la potenza di aspirazione. Si misura in pascal (Pa) , l'unità con cui si esprime la depressione creata dal motore: più il numero è alto, più il robot tira su sporco dai tappeti e dalle fughe . Nei modelli in offerta si va dai 7.000 Pa del 105 ai 30.000 Pa delle fasce più alte.

Il prezzo più basso del mese è quello del Roomba Combo 105 , a 149 euro, o 179 euro con base AutoEmpty . Anche il modello d'ingresso

Con pochi euro in più si entra nella nuova generazione. Il Roomba 115 Combo , nero o bianco, costa 169 euro è più piccolo della precedente generazione 105 in ogni dimensione : 24,5 centimetri di lato contro 33,6 e 9,2 di altezza contro 10,4, per appena 2,16 kg. Così si infila sotto più mobili, e intanto aspira con 15.000 Pa . La spazzola laterale pulisce a filo parete e anche il suo panno in microfibra si stacca e si lava. Con una carica copre fino a 84 metri quadrati, cioè un appartamento di medie dimensioni.

Ha la navigazione ClearView LiDAR e per il lavaggio usa un panno in microfibra, bagnato da una micropompa con tre livelli d'acqua da scegliere in base al pavimento. Quando riconosce un tappeto, la funzione Carpet Detect lo evita per non bagnarlo . Dall'app Roomba Home si impostano le routine e si sceglie quali stanze pulire per prime.

È uno dei prodotti di punta dell'offerta, e si capisce perché. Il Roomba 115 Combo con base AutoEmpty costa 219 euro e porta lo svuotamento automatico nella fascia d'ingresso.

Il robot è lo stesso 115 appena visto. La base però cambia l'uso quotidiano: a fine pulizia il Roomba rientra, la base aspira lo sporco dal contenitore e per circa tre mesi non serve toccarlo . Chi ha animali in casa, o chi semplicemente non vuole ritrovarsi ogni sera a svuotare un contenitore pieno di polvere, ha qui il modo più economico di dimenticarsene. È in vendita, nero o bianco, allo stesso prezzo.

Con la serie Plus 400 e 500 arriva la base AutoWash , e con lei un design più basso. I tre modelli sono alti appena 8,35 cm , con un profilo più sottile del 21% rispetto al Plus 505 della generazione precedente. In pratica passano più facilmente sotto letti, divani e mobili bassi, dove la polvere si accumula indisturbata.

Il lavaggio è affidato a due panni rotanti DualClean , che girano a 200 giri al minuto. La tecnologia SmartScrub aumenta la pressione sul pavimento contro lo sporco più ostinato , e quando il robot riconosce un tappeto solleva i panni di un centimetro per non bagnarlo.

Il Roomba Plus 415 Combo + AutoWash costa 349 euro e aspira con 20.000 Pa. Il Roomba Plus 515 Combo + AutoWash sale a 22.000 Pa e costa 399 euro. Entrambi sono disponibili neri o bianchi. Chi cerca la generazione precedente trova invece, sempre con base AutoWash , il Roomba Plus 405 Combo a 299 euro e il Plus 505 Combo a 399 euro.

Il secondo prodotto di punta del mese è il Roomba Plus 575 Combo + AutoWash , a 449 euro. Nero o bianco, conserva lo stesso profilo basso dei fratelli ma alza ogni dato.

L'aspirazione arriva a 25.000 Pa. La navigazione passa a ClearView Pro con PrecisionVision AI , una telecamera che riconosce gli oggetti sul pavimento, come cavi, scarpe e oggetti lasciati in giro, e li aggira invece di trascinarli. Anche la base fa un passo avanti: lava i panni con acqua a 75 °C e li asciuga con aria calda , così non restano umidi nella base fino al giro successivo, evitando muffe e cattivi odori.

Nella fascia alta cambia il modo di lavare, perché al posto dei panni rotanti c'è un rullo PowerSpin che strofina il pavimento con acqua calda a 60 °C e si pulisce da solo mentre lavora , premendo sul pavimento con una forza di 15 newton. Entrambi i modelli aspirano con 30.000 Pa, usano la navigazione ClearView Pro con PrecisionVision AI già vista sul 575 e sono alti 9,95 centimetri.

Il Roomba Plus 615 Combo , a 549 euro in nero, è la scelta di chi vuole il rullo lavapavimenti spendendo meno. La sua base Wash Only lava il rullo a 80 °C e lo asciuga, ma non svuota la polvere , che finisce in un sacchetto da un litro integrato nel robot, sufficiente per circa un mese.

Rispetto al 615 cambia la base, ed è la differenza che si sente di più. La AutoWash svuota la polvere, lava il rullo a 80 °C, lo asciuga con aria a 55 °C e dosa da sola il detergente . Si va avanti fino a 90 giorni senza interventi .

Il Roomba Plus 675 Combo + AutoWash è il terzo prodotto di punta del mese. Costa 599 euro ed è disponibile bianco o nero.

Sul robot la tecnologia PerfectEdge allunga il rullo verso i bordi per arrivare fino al battiscopa , e la spazzola anti-groviglio non resta avvolta dai peli degli animali (ha un meccanismo taglia-peli che li accorcia mentre gira, così non c'è da liberarla a mano con le forbici).

La serie Max è quella pensata per le case più movimentate, con bambini, animali e tanti tappeti. In offerta c'è il Roomba Max 705 Combo + AutoWash , bianco, a 599 euro. Lava con il rullo PowerSpin già visto sui Plus 615 e 675, protetto da una copertura che tiene asciutti i tappeti mentre il robot li attraversa, e aspira con 13.000 Pa e due spazzole in gomma anti-groviglio. La funzione Dirt Detect riconosce le zone più sporche , mentre Carpet Boost alza in automatico la potenza quando il robot sale su un tappeto .

Con PrecisionVision AI il 705 riconosce cavi e calzini, e perfino i bisogni degli animali domestici , e li aggira.

La base AutoWash lava e asciuga il rullo con acqua e aria calde , dosa da sola il detergente e svuota la polvere per 75 giorni.

Chi ha soprattutto tappeti e non ha bisogno del lavaggio può guardare al Roomba Max 715 Vac + AutoEmpty , a 449 euro in nero. È un aspirapolvere puro, con 30.000 Pa , le due spazzole in gomma anti-groviglio, Dirt Detect, Carpet Boost e la base AutoEmpty.

L'ultimo prodotto di punta è il modello più completo dell'offerta. Il Roomba Max 775 Combo + AutoWash costa 699 euro.

Riunisce quello che si è visto fin qui e si presenta come il più complet o. Aspira con 30.000 Pa, ha le due spazzole in gomma, Dirt Detect e Carpet Boost degli altri Max, e lava con il rullo PowerSpin, protetto dalla stessa copertura per i tappeti. La base AutoWash svuota lo sporco fino a tre mesi, lava il rullo a 75 °C, lo asciuga a 50 °C, dosa il detergente e rabbocca l'acqua . La navigazione è ClearView Pro con PrecisionVision AI, come sul 705.

Da oggi, 6 Roomba sono in offerta anche su Amazon, con prezzi in qualche caso più bassi di quelli di irobot.it. Tra questi ci sono le versioni 416, 516 e 576: sono le versioni proposte su Amazon dei Plus 415, 515 e 575, con le stesse caratteristiche tecniche.

items.title: Barcolana, the world’s most pop sailing race
items.summary: Europe’s biggest celebration of the sea returns to Trieste. Already a Guinness World Record holder, 2026 Barcolana regatta brings together 500 events, a packed programme of races and a sailing village in the heart of the city
items.content:
Got a sailing boat? Then you can take part. Barcolana, Europe’s biggest celebration of the sea, is taking over Trieste, on Italy’s eastern border, the former multicultural port of the Habsburg Empire. More than 500 events are scheduled across over 100 locations, on land, in the lagoon and, of course, at sea. Yet this huge event, which entered the Guinness World Records as the world’s largest sailing race, with 2,689 boats registered in 2018, began almost by chance.

In 1969, a small group of friends, the founders of the Società Velica di Barcola e Grignano sailing club, came up with the magic formula over drinks in a bar. No handicaps, no measurement rules, no ratings: everyone races together and the first boat across the line wins. Fifty-one boats took part.

Barcolana grew year after year. It became the place where world-class champions race alongside occasional sailors; where spectacular maxi yachts line up at the start alongside tiny boats whose galleys resemble neighbourhood taverns; where sailing belongs to everyone and is open to everyone. Or, as British sailing legend Sir Ben Ainslie put it: “Something I’ve never done before.”

For the ten days of Barcolana, Trieste — the city just a stone’s throw from Slovenia where James Joyce worked as an English teacher, journalist, clerk, singing student and translator — becomes sailing’s “pop” capital.

Piazza Unità d’Italia, Europe’s largest square overlooking the sea, with its buildings reflecting the splendour of the Habsburg era, becomes the heart of the event. And the Rive — Trieste’s waterfront, linking the city centre to the sea — are transformed into a village built around sailors, with an astonishing number of stands selling everything from local food and DOC wines to clothing and sailing equipment.

But the village itself is constantly evolving. Year after year it expands, taking over new parts of the city, because by now the Barcolana is all-encompassing.

The sea, however, remains the undisputed star. And the highlight, bringing the festival to a close, is always the historic international sailing race held on the second Sunday in October.

On Sunday 11 October, the starting gun fires at 10.30am. The 13-mile course forms a quadrilateral, with the finish line off Piazza Unità. The most spectacular moment is the start itself, when the water seems to disappear beneath an endless expanse of sails — tiny, small, large and enormous.

Barcolana, of course, has a champion to beat. Furio Benussi’s 100-foot maxi yacht Arca SGR has won the most recent editions and is now chasing yet another consecutive victory.

Benussi, Arca SGR ’s owner and skipper, is Triestino through and through.

He races in his home waters and has the record of a true champion, with world, European and Italian titles to his name. He also belongs to a sailing dynasty: his brother Gabriele is a renowned tactician, while his daughter Marta is carrying on the family tradition.

Barcolana is never short of big names. This year they include James Spithill, a two-time America’s Cup winner; Ivica Kostelić, the former world champion skier turned offshore sailor; and Olympic swimmer Luca Dotto.

And then there is Wendy Schmidt, the American philanthropist and sailor who became the first woman to win the race, aboard Deep Blue . “La Wendy”, as the people of Trieste call her — they have more or less adopted her as one of their own — is back with two initiatives designed to promote greater knowledge and protection of the ocean.

The first is the Deep Blue Exploration Zone , an interactive science pavilion focusing on biodiversity and blue carbon. The second is the immersive tunnel experience The Ocean in Me , a ten-minute journey that begins in space and descends into the ocean depths, with images captured by the Schmidt Ocean Institute’s underwater robot. Both can be found in Piazza Unità.

The ten-day programme, built around the theme “Be Barcolana” and a 2026 campaign image by Serse Roma, is packed. Races and sporting events follow one another at such a pace that it is impossible to list them all.

There is a swimming race, a stand-up paddleboarding competition, the Women in Sailing by Generali regatta — backed by the insurance giant that has long supported Barcolana — and the Classic regatta, where vintage yachts compete against one another.

There are also the “boats of legality”, night races and, as guest of honour, the Amerigo Vespucci , the Italian Navy’s training ship, regarded by many as the most beautiful ship in the world.

But Barcolana is not just about the sea. On land, too, the programme is vast. There is, for example, the Un mare di racconti literary festival, as well as exhibitions, concerts and talks. The Sea Summit conference focuses on artificial intelligence for the maritime world and the blue economy, while there is even a Barcolana SKI event featuring Kristian Ghedina and Tina Maze.

At the helm of this vast operation is Mitja Gialuz, president of the Società Velica di Barcola e Grignano, but the organisation involves more than a thousand people, including a huge number of volunteers.

One piece of advice? If you happen to be in Trieste during Barcolana, simply head down to Piazza Unità, walk along the waterfront, wander through the streets of the centre or even venture out into the suburbs.

You won’t need to look for Barcolana. Barcolana will find you.

items.title: Rome’s Via dei Fori Imperiali: a new pedestrian boulevard among ancient ruins
items.summary: Cars will be removed, improving visitors’ access to the site. Ancient squares, such as Trajan’s Forum, will once again be accessible on foot
items.content:
ROME — Via dei Fori Imperiali, Rome’s historic monumental avenue linking the Colosseum to Piazza Venezia, is set to be transformed by summer 2027. The road through the ruins of imperial Rome — today something of an urban motorway, as wide as a six-lane road — will become “a pedestrian boulevard”, in the words of Rome’s mayor, Roberto Gualtieri. The pavements will disappear and a series of pedestrian terraces will be built directly overlooking the temples and columns erected by Caesar and Augustus.

Ancient squares, including Trajan’s Forum, will once again be accessible on foot after almost 2,000 years. Romans and tourists will be able to get closer to the monuments, coming within touching distance of the columns of the Temple of Mars and the archaeological complexes commissioned by Caesar and Augustus.

The work is part of CArMe — Rome Monumental Archaeological Centre — the largest urban regeneration and archaeological heritage enhancement programme ever undertaken in the heart of the Italian capital.

CArMe covers a vast area stretching from Piazza Venezia to the Imperial Forums, from the Colosseum to the Palatine Hill, and from the Caelian Hill to the Baths of Caracalla, the Circus Maximus and the Capitoline Hill. Total investment in projects currently under way amounts to around €200 million.

The new archaeological promenade — linking the city’s main monuments and making them more accessible — is one of the project’s most significant elements. It includes, in particular, the gradual transformation of Via dei Fori Imperiali.

Mayor Gualtieri and Claudio Parisi Presicce, Rome’s superintendent for cultural heritage, say the aim is twofold: to encourage Romans to return to the heart of their city, an area too often left to foreign visitors and overwhelmed by mass tourism, while at the same time reconnecting the historic city with contemporary Rome.

A site visit to the the world-famous avenue reveals both the benefits and the limitations of the partial pedestrianisation inherited from the past. Private cars have now been banned from the heart of ancient Rome, removing the Colosseum’s 20th-century role as a traffic roundabout But taxis, official vehicles and buses still speed along the avenue.

This situation effectively forces pedestrians to crowd onto the old pavements on either side, away from vehicles travelling along the road at very high speed, effectively undermining the original goal of pedestrianisation.

Under the new plan, only two central lanes will be reserved for buses and taxis. They will be marked out visually by small metal studs, encouraging pedestrians to reclaim the central part of the avenue.The redevelopment will also see the return of the pine trees removed in recent years, while many new trees of different species will be planted along the road.

The first work on Via dei Fori Imperiali began last spring, with the removal and relaying of the sampietrini, the traditional dark stone blocks used to pave the streets of Rome’s historic centre.The new design features broad transverse veins of travertine echoing the perimeter walls of ancient temples that were demolished.

At the Piazza Venezia end, the road is already finished, with the stone blocks once again fitted neatly into place. Further towards the Colosseum, however, the avenue remains a noisy construction site as the final work continues on Metro Line C. Road paving here is due to be completed by the end of 2026.

The first terraces overlooking the Roman Forum are due to be completed by January 2027, along with a new pedestrian bridge that will run beside the Forums and link the Monti district to the Mamertine Prison, the ancient Roman jail that held some of its most prominent prisoners.

“By March 2027,” Gualtieri says, “the existing pavements will be removed. They will be replaced by basalt paving laid flush with the sampietrini elsewhere on the carriageway. Finally, by the summer, the remaining terraces on the Imperial Forums side will be completed.”

The new paving will extend six metres beyond the road’s current footprint. The mayor stresses, however, that local public transport can only be removed from the area once the Venezia station on Line C, Rome’s third metro line, has been fully completed.

Another priority is tackling a long-standing blight on the appearance of the area: the souvenir stalls, which were still clearly visible during the latest official inspections. Rome City Council is currently working on a new plan designed to address previous objections raised by the regional administrative court and permanently put an end to the sale of trinkets in the area by 2027.

And there is more. The mayor says the large municipal building on Via dei Cerchi will become the new Museum of the City of Rome, while work will begin in January to remove the low wall along the Circus Maximus, creating a direct connection with the Palatine Hill. Twenty service centres are also planned, along with a new information point in front of the Basilica of Maxentius.

A new Antiquarium on the Caelian Hill will open to the public in the coming months. Work will also soon begin to pedestrianise the final stretch of Via Cavour — the major thoroughfare that intersects Via dei Fori Imperiali — turning it into a key gateway to Rome’s central archaeological area.

Among the projects already completed is the restoration of the square of Trajan’s Forum, the largest forum in the ancient world. Presicce says the aim is to make it accessible to today’s public: “And to make that possible, walkable marble slabs will soon be laid.”

items.title: Keith Haring: chalk, colour and the pulse of New York
items.summary: A major exhibition at the Museo di Roma celebrates the pop artist, on view until 11 April 2027
items.content:
ROME – You can almost hear the rap music, the rumble of the New York subway, the hum of crowds moving through the streets of Tribeca. You can almost see a young Keith Haring at work, rapidly drawing with his chalk. Now the great pop artist is the subject of a major solo exhibition at the Museo di Roma — a symbolic return to the city that welcomed him in 1984, when he created a joyous magenta mural on the Palazzo delle Esposizioni, later erased during restoration of the façade.

The exhibition at Palazzo Braschi, open to the public until 11 April 2027, has been curated by Kaoru Yanase, Ilaria Miarelli Mariani and Claudio Zambianchi. It traces Haring’s eventful and, sadly, brief career. The artist died of AIDS in 1990 at just 31.

He was still a young man. And this exhibition feels like a journey through the life of a twenty-something graffiti artist: colourful, vibrant, dazzling and explosive. He was the Chalkman , frenetically covering subway stations with the symbols that would become global icons.

As curator Ilaria Miarelli Mariani explains: “Haring wanted above all to speak to children, which is why he used a colourful, simple language that was as universal as possible. He believed children possessed a purity that was somehow eroded as they grew up. That is why he used the Radiant Baby , one of his most important tags, everywhere. The Dog , on the other hand, represented violence, the police and obtuseness.”

She adds: “All these works — more than 140 pieces including sculptures, posters, record covers, paintings, car bonnets and a motorcycle — come together to form a manifesto for an era, and their impact remains incredibly powerful today.”

You can feel the electricity of the 1980s. Haring’s brilliant colours dominate every room of Palazzo Braschi, creating an immersive journey in which yellow, blue and red walls contrast with the historic floors and frescoed ceilings of what was once the home of Luigi Braschi Onesti, nephew of Pope Pius VI.

The exhibition seeks to reconstruct Haring’s visual grammar. In Icons , the 1990 series bringing together some of his most famous figures — the Radiant Baby , Angel , Dog and Winged Man — Haring created an alphabet that anyone could read.

In the section devoted to his political and social activism, posters and works such as Free South Africa , Crack Down! and Safe Sex! turn art into powerful messages against racism, apartheid, nuclear war and AIDS.

The exhibition then moves on to Radiant Eros – Celebrate Life and works including the Bad Boys panels and the monumental Untitled from 1984, made with fluorescent pigments and displayed under black light, before reaching The Serpent , The Cross , The Angel and The Pyramid .

It culminates with Apocalypse and Altarpiece: The Life of Christ , two works in which Haring, already ill, confronts death more directly. The exhibition ends with the mantra that guided his entire body of work: “Art is for everybody.”

Museo di Roma at Palazzo Braschi, Piazza San Pantaleo 10 – Piazza Navona 2

items.title: Luca Marinelli: “I’m not afraid of disappearing”
items.summary: Now starring in The Echo Chamber, based on the last story written by Bernardo Bertolucci, the Italian actor talks about vulnerability, solitude — including that of prime numbers — and freedom on a sunny day in Berlin, the city he has called home for the past few years
items.content:
Luca Marinelli is happy to rediscover his vulnerability, proud to acknowledge his shyness and aware that he may fail. The extraordinary thing, for him, is simply to be ordinary.

Wary of self-satisfaction and anything that might smack of narcissism, when he talks about his character he often uses the phrase “basically” — as if to sketch out a frame, a point of reference, a certain disposition, but never a fixed identity. Because we move, we change, and we are never quite the same person.

The rest is experience, calluses on your hands and luck. “I’ve certainly been very lucky. But I went looking for that luck, and I pursued it with determination.”

Andrea Pallaoro, the director of The Echo Chamber, has cast him in a taut, enigmatic chamber drama in which the characters move around an apartment that feels like a prison to which no one has the key.

Written by Ludovica Rampoldi, Ilaria Bernardini and Bernardo Bertolucci, the screenplay echoes the idea that once inspired Last Tango in Paris: “To keep everything shut inside a room — love, suffering, pleasure. Without hurting anyone, without revealing anything about yourself and without knowing anything about the other person. Nothing more than two people in a state of grace.”

It gives Marinelli, Alicia Vikander and Susan Sarandon the space to turn a look into words and, amid a desperate inability to master pain, make silence more powerful than any speech.

“The audience knows nothing about the character I play, yet somehow it knows everything. Andrea Pallaoro’s great achievement, and his extraordinary artistry, was to shoot a film in a single room and turn that room into an entire world. And the audience is there too, invisible, spying on this couple, almost as though sitting beside them or peering through a half-open door. You hear their sighs, feel the vibrations, share in their torments and their storms. There is so much to understand and to tell, but the wonderful thing is that nothing needs explaining. Everything is there to be seen, right in front of you.”

The sun is shining in Berlin, where Marinelli has lived for several years. Paintings and photographs punctuate the sweep of an enormous bookcase. Mino, his dog, has taken possession of the sofa and barks at regular intervals, just to remind us he is there.

“The younger you are, the more you suffer and the harder you try to find your own voice. I don’t think there’s anything special about me. I think it happens to everyone.”

And now that you’ve crossed the forty-year threshold? “My suffering has changed, become something else, because I’ve learnt to know myself and I try to shed the things that used to weigh me down.”

Was shyness one of those burdens? “It was simply a fact. As far back as I can remember, I’ve always been shy.”

Shy, but with something of a contradiction there too. Jonathan Safran Foer says shyness means looking away from something you desire. Perhaps acting was no accident. “That’s true, there is a contradiction. But it’s as though, once I enter the game of acting, I throw myself into it because I love playing that game so much. It can take very little to make me feel out of place, and even there, on stage or on set, I can suddenly lose that sense of confidence.”

Does that bother you? “Not at all. Feeling unsettled is vital. It keeps you present, aware of yourself. It’s profoundly human.”

And then? “And then, if you do this job — anyone who says otherwise is talking bullshit — there is a desire to be seen, to be noticed.”

Is that enough? “Of course not. When I act, I have this ambition to communicate, to show you a side of myself, to show you what that story has passed on to me. It’s like being thrown onto a stage, with a melody playing in the background, and someone saying: ‘Now dance.’”

And you dance in your own way. “Every actor does. Leonardo, the character I play in The Echo Chamber, would have struck different notes if you or anyone else had played him. I put into him what I’ve seen and felt over all these years.”

What do you think when you watch yourself on screen? “I always watch them twice. The first time as a merciless critic of myself, the second more or less as a member of the audience.”

The Echo Chamber was in competition at Venice, just like your first film, The Solitude of Prime Numbers. Sixteen years have passed. “With Alba Rohrwacher and Saverio Costanzo, I felt like a complete beginner. It was my first film and I knew nothing. They would talk about cinema, mention films and influences, and I’d nod along pretending I knew every reference because I couldn’t bring myself to admit how ignorant I was. Then I’d go home and study. I had piles of films on my desk. That period was an incredibly important education for me, and Alba and Saverio were two great teachers.”

You auditioned twice for the film. “I did the first audition and wasn’t happy with it. I don’t think they had rejected me, but they were seeing a lot of actors. Then I read the book and gathered my courage. I went into an internet café and emailed Jorgelina DePretis, the casting director: ‘Please, give me a second chance.’ Sadly, she’s no longer with us, but she was a wonderful colleague whom I loved very much.”

And you got that second chance. “By then I thought I’d missed my chance. Then the phone rang and they called me back: luck and a bit of determination.”

How old were you when cinema first captivated you? “My father used to take me to the theatre and my mother to the cinema. The movie theatre became this magical place. As a kid, I watched everything. I was captivated by bodies, actions, sounds, kisses, wars, embraces. I fell in love, I cried, I got carried away as though I were living those adventures myself. Cinema has meant many different things in my life, and all of them have been important.”

Did watching so many films help you? “Are you kidding? It was like carrying an instruction manual around in my pocket, and having an inexhaustible source of wonder. When I think about the way Leone chooses to end Once Upon a Time in America, I’m still astonished. De Niro is crooked, unlikely, almost unpresentable in that unexpected smile. But he does it. He gives himself over to it. He makes himself available. He allows himself to be guided and puts one of his thousand faces at the service of a masterpiece. That’s where the greatness of an actor lies: in that act of creative freedom, in taking that risk.”

What does the word freedom make you think of? “My happy childhoods in the Rieti area. In Longone Sabino, nobody thought about having to be reachable all the time. We were kids dropped into this tiny village where the days were marked only by lunch and dinner. If you didn’t turn up, people started worrying, but otherwise we were free. Streams, swimming holes, woods, ravines, evenings under the stars on benches, video games in the village’s only bar in summer. Then snow, snowmen and racing down hills on sledges in winter. I loved the city too, but life in a smaller place worked completely differently.”

How did you manage to fail a school year twice? “What can I tell you? I’m certainly not going to sit here now and put my teachers on trial.”

Was it entirely your fault? “Shall we call it a democratic fifty-fifty? I did have some interests — Greek literature, for a start — but I wasn’t particularly motivated. Schools have a responsibility to try to meet the person in front of them where they are. Mine didn’t really do that with me, and so I ended up repeating two years.”

How would you describe your family? “Crazy and wonderful. What do you call it? Middle class? On my father’s side, I saw people working in the arts; on my mother’s, people doing practical jobs — office work, dressmaking, carpentry, which is another form of art. I owe my parents a great deal in many ways: humanity, seriousness, sensitivity and a certain amount of madness too. When I said, ‘I want to be an actor,’ they didn’t have me committed. They supported me. I’m still enormously grateful to them.”

“I see the ball coming towards me like a locomotive, and I am alone in the sky as I fly towards the shot while you hold your breath.” Umberto Saba is writing about the goalkeeper. “I know what he means because I used to play in goal, and I still do. I started very late, when I was sixteen, but I love football because, like cinema, it’s a team game.”

Alessandro Borghi, whom you have often acted with, says you have an enormous talent that “exists independently of ego and self-awareness”. “We’re like brothers. I feel safe with him. I know that if I pass him the ball, even if I don’t play it perfectly, he’ll score.”

You and Borghi shared more than a film set. You also went through the almost mystical experience of making Claudio Caligari’s final film, Don’t Be Bad. (He gets up, shows me a photograph of himself with Caligari, then sits down again.) “Claudio was an incredibly sweet, passionate man who could be very direct.”

Does direct mean brusque? “It means direct. And I liked that about him, because clarity illuminates things. You immediately understand what the other person is looking for.”
